- Plants serve as a primary sink for \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) via photosynthesis, not \(\mathrm{CO}\).
- Oceans primarily absorb \(\mathrm{CO}_2\).
- Haemoglobin binds \(\mathrm{CO}\) in living organisms causing toxicity, but is not an environmental sink.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Micro-organisms present in the soil are a sink for \(\mathrm{CO}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q53 - Product of self aldol condensation of cyclohexanone followed by heating

questiontext.text: Of the following, which is the product formed when cyclohexanone undergoes aldol condensation followed by heating?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Reactant and Conditions
- Reactant: Cyclohexanone
- Reaction: Self-aldol condensation followed by heating (dehydration)

Step 2: Reaction Mechanism
- Deprotonation of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen in cyclohexanone forms an enolate ion.
- Enolate attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second cyclohexanone molecule to form a \(\beta\)-hydroxy ketone intermediate.
- Heating induces dehydration (loss of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)) to yield an \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated cyclic ketone: 2-(cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)cyclohexan-1-one.

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
- The dehydrated product contains a double bond linking the two six-membered rings directly adjacent to the carbonyl carbon.
- The structure corresponding to 2-(cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)cyclohexan-1-one is the correct product.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q54 - Isoelectronic and isostructural molecular pair

questiontext.text: Which of the following pair of compounds is isoelectronic and isostructural?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definitions
- Isoelectronic species have the same total number of valence electrons.
- Isostructural species have the same molecular geometry/shape and central atom hybridization.

Step 2: Evaluation of \(\mathrm{IBr}_2^-\) and \(\mathrm{XeF}_2\)
- Valence electrons in \(\mathrm{IBr}_2^-\): \(7\text{ (I)} + 2 \times 7\text{ (Br)} + 1\text{ (charge)} = 22\text{ electrons}\).
- Valence electrons in \(\mathrm{XeF}_2\): \(8\text{ (Xe)} + 2 \times 7\text{ (F)} = 22\text{ electrons}\).
- Both species are isoelectronic with 22 valence electrons.
- Central iodine in \(\mathrm{IBr}_2^-\) has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs (\(\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}\) hybridization), resulting in linear molecular geometry.
- Central xenon in \(\mathrm{XeF}_2\) has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs (\(\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}\) hybridization), resulting in linear molecular geometry.
- Both species are linear and isostructural.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pair \(\mathrm{IBr}_2^-\) and \(\mathrm{XeF}_2\) is both isoelectronic and isostructural.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q55 - Identification of organic reaction sequence intermediates and products

questiontext.text:
Consider the reactions:

Identify A, X, Y and Z

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction Sequence Analysis
- \(X\) has molecular formula \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_6\mathrm{O}\). Dehydrogenation over \(\mathrm{Cu}\) at \(573\text{ K}\) yields compound \(A\). Thus, \(X\) is Ethanol (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\)).
- Oxidation/dehydrogenation of ethanol gives ethanal (acetaldehyde, \(A = \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CHO}\)).
- Ethanal reduces Tollen's reagent \([\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2]^+\) to form a silver mirror.
- Self-aldol condensation of ethanal (\(A\)) in presence of dilute \(\mathrm{OH}^-\) and heating yields \(Y = \text{but-2-enal}\) (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCHO}\)).
- Reaction of ethanal (\(A\)) with semicarbazide (\(\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{NHCONH}_2\)) produces semicarbazone (\(Z = \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{N-NHCONH}_2\)).

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The identity of the compounds is: A = Ethanal, X = Ethanol, Y = But-2-enal, Z = Semicarbazone.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q56 - Comparison of acidity among phenolic derivatives

questiontext.text: Which one is the most acidic compound?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acidity of phenolic compounds depends on the stability of the conjugate phenoxide anion formed after deprotonation. Electron-withdrawing groups stabilize phenoxide through inductive (-I) and resonance (-M) effects, increasing acidity.

Step 2: Analysis of Compounds
- 4-methylphenol has an electron-donating methyl group (+I, hyperconjugation), decreasing acidity relative to phenol.
- Phenol lacks substituents.
- 4-nitrophenol contains one electron-withdrawing nitro group (-I, -M), increasing acidity.
- 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid) contains three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups at ortho and para positions (-I, -M), extraordinarily stabilizing the phenoxide ion through multiple resonance structures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
2,4,6-Trinitrophenol is the most acidic compound.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q57 - Gas that decolourizes acidified potassium permanganate solution

questiontext.text: Name the gas that can readily decolourizes acidified \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) solution.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acidified \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) is a strong oxidizing agent (purple color due to \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\)). Reducing gases decolorize it by reducing \(\mathrm{Mn}^{7+}\) to colorless \(\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Options
- Sulfur dioxide (\(\mathrm{SO}_2\)) acts as a strong reducing agent in aqueous medium.
- Reaction equation:
\[ 2 \mathrm{MnO}_4^- + 5 \mathrm{SO}_2 + 2 \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + 5 \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} + 4 \mathrm{H}^+ \]
- \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) and \(\mathrm{P}_2\mathrm{O}_5\) are in their highest oxidation states and do not act as reducing agents.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{SO}_2\) gas readily decolorizes acidified \(\mathrm{KMnO}_4\) solution.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q58 - Correct order of acidity among hydrocarbons

questiontext.text: Which one is the correct order of acidity?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acidity of hydrocarbons increases with increasing s-character of the carbon atom bonded to hydrogen, as greater s-character increases electronegativity and stabilizes the conjugate acetylide/carbanion base.

Step 2: Analysis of Hydrocarbon Hybridization
- Ethyne (\(\mathrm{HC}\equiv\mathrm{CH}\)): \(\mathrm{sp}\) hybridized C (\(50\%\) s-character), most acidic.
- Propyne (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH}\)): \(\mathrm{sp}\) hybridized terminal C, but electron-donating methyl group (+I effect) reduces acidity relative to ethyne.
- Ethene (\(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}_2\)): \(\mathrm{sp}^2\) hybridized C (\(33.3\%\) s-character).
- Ethane (\(\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_3\)): \(\mathrm{sp}^3\) hybridized C (\(25\%\) s-character), least acidic.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct order of acidity is \(\mathrm{HC}\equiv\mathrm{CH} > \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{C}\equiv\mathrm{CH} > \mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}_2 > \mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{CH}_3\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q59 - Solubility product calculation for silver oxalate

questiontext.text: Concentration of the \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) ions in a saturated solution of \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4\) is \(2.2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\). Solubility product of \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4\) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Concentration of silver ions \([\mathrm{Ag}^+] = 2.2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
- Dissociation equilibrium for sparingly soluble salt \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4\):
\[ \mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Ag}^+(aq) + \mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}(aq) \]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
- Stoichiometric relation: \([\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}] = \frac{1}{2} [\mathrm{Ag}^+]\)
- Solubility product expression: \(K_{sp} = [\mathrm{Ag}^+]^2 [\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}]\)

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- Calculate oxalate ion concentration:
\[ [\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}] = \frac{2.2 \times 10^{-4}}{2} = 1.1 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1} \]
- Calculate \(K_{sp}\):
\[ K_{sp} = (2.2 \times 10^{-4})^2 \times (1.1 \times 10^{-4}) \]
\[ K_{sp} = (4.84 \times 10^{-8}) \times (1.1 \times 10^{-4}) = 5.324 \times 10^{-12} \approx 5.3 \times 10^{-12} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
- Dimensional analysis confirms \(K_{sp}\) has units of \(\text{mol}^3 \text{L}^{-3}\).
- The solubility product of \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4\) is \(5.3 \times 10^{-12}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q60 - True statement regarding conformers of ethane

questiontext.text: With respect to the conformers of ethane, which of the following statements is true?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Conformers (conformational isomers) of ethane are produced by rotation around the carbon-carbon single (\(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}\)) \(\sigma\)-bond.

Step 2: Analysis of Structural Parameters
- Rotation about the single bond alters only the dihedral angle (torsional angle) between the hydrogen atoms on adjacent carbon atoms.
- Intramolecular \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bond lengths, \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}\) bond length, and \(\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) / \(\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}\) bond angles remain strictly constant during rotation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both bond angles and bond lengths remain the same across different conformers of ethane.

answer.text: Both bond angles and bond length remains same.
Bond angle remains same but bond length changes.
Bond angle changes but bond length remains same.
Both bond angle and bond length change.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q61 - Definition and properties of an electrophile

questiontext.text: The correct statement regarding electrophile is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electrophiles are electron-loving species (Lewis acids) that possess an incomplete octet or an empty orbital capable of accepting a pair of electrons.

Step 2: Evaluation of Characteristics
- Electrophiles can be positively charged ions (such as \(\mathrm{H}^+\), \(\mathrm{NO}_2^+\), \(\mathrm{R}^+\)) or neutral molecules with vacant orbitals (such as \(\mathrm{BF}_3\), \(\mathrm{AlCl}_3\)).
- During a chemical reaction, an electrophile accepts an electron pair from an electron-rich nucleophile to form a covalent bond.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
An electrophile can be either a neutral or positively charged species and forms a bond by accepting an electron pair from a nucleophile.

answer.text: Electrophile can be either neutral or positively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile.
Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from another electro-phile
Electrophiles are generally neutral species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q62 - Identification of incorrect statement in atomic structure

questiontext.text: Which one is the wrong statement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Atomic Structure
Evaluation of orbital energies, de-Broglie wavelength, Heisenberg uncertainty principle, and exchange energy stability.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
- For single-electron hydrogen-like species, energy depends solely on the principal quantum number \(n\). Therefore, \(2s\) and \(2p\) orbitals are degenerate (\(E_{2s} = E_{2p}\)). Stating that \(2s\) has lower energy than \(2p\) in hydrogen-like atoms is incorrect.
- de-Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = \frac{h}{m v}\) is valid.
- Heisenberg uncertainty principle in terms of energy and time \(\Delta E \times \Delta t \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}\) is valid.
- Half-filled and fully-filled subshells exhibit enhanced stability due to exchange energy and symmetrical distribution.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement claiming \(2s\) orbital energy is less than \(2p\) orbital energy in hydrogen-like atoms is incorrect.

answer.text: The energy of \(2s\) orbital is less than the energy of \(2p\) orbital in case of Hydrogen like atoms.
de-Broglie's wavelength is given by \(\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}\) where \(m =\) mass of the particle, \(v =\) group velocity of the particle.
Half-filled and fully filled orbitals have greater stability due to greater exchange energy, greater symmetry and more balanced arrangement.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q63 - Absorption wavelength order for cobalt 3 plus coordination complexes

questiontext.text: Correct increasing order for the wavelengths of absorption in the visible region for the complexes of \(\text{Co}^{3+}\) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Principle
- Complexes of \(\mathrm{Co}^{3+}\): \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3]^{3+}\), \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\), and \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+}\).
- Crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta_o\)) depends on ligand field strength according to the spectrochemical series.

Step 2: Analysis of Ligand Field Strength
- Order of ligand strength: \(\mathrm{en} > \mathrm{NH}_3 > \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\).
- Corresponding crystal field splitting energy order:
\[ \Delta_o([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3]^{3+}) > \Delta_o([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}) > \Delta_o([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+}) \]

Step 3: Relation to Absorption Wavelength
- Energy of absorbed photon: \(E = \frac{h c}{\lambda} = \Delta_o \implies \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\Delta_o}\).
- Therefore, stronger ligand field splitting corresponds to shorter absorption wavelength.
- Increasing order of absorption wavelength:
\[ [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3]^{3+} < [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+} < [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+} \]

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct increasing order of absorption wavelength is \([\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_3]^{3+}, [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}, [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{3+}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q64 - Matching interhalogen compound types with geometries

questiontext.text:
Match the interhalogen compounds of column I with the geometry in column II and assign the correct code.

Column - IColumn - II
(A) \(\text{XX}'\)(i) T-shape
(B) \(\text{XX}'_3\)(ii) Pentagonal bipyramidal
(C) \(\text{XX}'_5\)(iii) Linear
(D) \(\text{XX}'_7\)(iv) Square-pyramidal
(v) Tetrahedral

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Application of VSEPR Theory
- \(\mathrm{XX}'\): Diatomic interhalogen molecule with linear geometry \(\rightarrow\) (iii).
- \(\mathrm{XX}'_3\): Central atom has 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs (\(\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}\) hybridization), forming a T-shaped geometry \(\rightarrow\) (i).
- \(\mathrm{XX}'_5\): Central atom has 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair (\(\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^2\) hybridization), forming a square-pyramidal geometry \(\rightarrow\) (iv).
- \(\mathrm{XX}'_7\): Central atom has 7 bond pairs + 0 lone pairs (\(\mathrm{sp}^3\mathrm{d}^3\) hybridization), forming a pentagonal bipyramidal geometry \(\rightarrow\) (ii).

Step 2: Matching Code
(A) \(\rightarrow\) (iii), (B) \(\rightarrow\) (i), (C) \(\rightarrow\) (iv), (D) \(\rightarrow\) (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching code sequence is (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q65 - Species with 120 degree bond angles

questiontext.text: The species, having bond angles of \(120^\circ\) is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Molecular Hybridization and Geometry
- \(\mathrm{BCl}_3\): Central boron has 3 valence electrons, forming 3 bond pairs with chlorine atoms and 0 lone pairs. Hybridization is \(\mathrm{sp}^2\), giving a trigonal planar geometry with bond angles of \(120^\circ\).
- \(\mathrm{PH}_3\): Central phosphorus has 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, displaying a pyramidal geometry with bond angles close to \(93.5^\circ\).
- \(\mathrm{ClF}_3\): Central chlorine has 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, displaying T-shaped geometry with bond angles close to \(87.5^\circ\).
- \(\mathrm{NCl}_3\): Central nitrogen has 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, displaying trigonal pyramidal geometry with bond angles around \(107^\circ\).

Step 2: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{BCl}_3\) is the species possessing \(120^\circ\) bond angles.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q66 - Increasing order of basic strength of substituted anilines

questiontext.text:
The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds is

(I)

(II)

(III)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Basic strength of aromatic amines depends on the availability of the unshared electron pair on the nitrogen atom to accept a proton. Electron-donating groups (+I, hyperconjugation) increase basicity, whereas electron-withdrawing groups (-I, -M) decrease basicity.

Step 2: Comparative Analysis
- Structure (II) 4-nitroaniline: Contains a strong electron-withdrawing nitro group (\(-\mathrm{NO}_2\)) at para-position (-I and -M effect), which delocalizes nitrogen lone pair electrons into the ring and lowers basicity significantly.
- Structure (I) Aniline: Unsubstituted aromatic amine.
- Structure (III) 4-methylaniline: Contains an electron-donating methyl group (\(-\mathrm{CH}_3\)) at para-position (+I and hyperconjugation effect), which increases electron density on nitrogen, making it the most basic.
- Combining these effects gives the increasing basicity order: \(\text{II} < \text{I} < \text{III}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct order of basic strength is \(\text{II} < \text{I} < \text{III}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q67 - Identification of incorrect statement regarding catalysts and enzymes

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Catalysis
A catalyst accelerates a chemical reaction by providing an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
- Coenzymes act as non-protein organic activators that enhance enzyme catalytic activity.
- A catalyst cannot initiate a non-spontaneous reaction; it only speeds up a thermodynamically feasible process.
- A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions equally. Consequently, it helps attain equilibrium faster without changing the value of the equilibrium constant (\(K_{\text{eq}}\)). Thus, claiming that the equilibrium constant value is changed by a catalyst is incorrect.
- Enzymes are biological catalysts that mediate biochemical reactions.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement claiming that the value of equilibrium constant is changed in the presence of a catalyst is incorrect.

answer.text: Coenzymes increase the catalytic activity of enzyme.
The value of equilibrium constant is changed in the presence of a catalyst in the reaction at equilibrium.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q68 - Internal energy change during adiabatic gas expansion

questiontext.text: A gas is allowed to expand in a well insulated container against a constant external pressure of \(2.5\text{ atm}\) from an initial volume of \(2.50\text{ L}\) to a final volume of \(4.50\text{ L}\). The change in internal energy \(\Delta U\) of the gas in joules will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Constant external pressure \(P_{\text{ext}} = 2.5\text{ atm}\)
- Initial volume \(V_1 = 2.50\text{ L}\)
- Final volume \(V_2 = 4.50\text{ L}\)
- Container is well insulated \(\implies q = 0\) (adiabatic process)
- Conversion factor: \(1\text{ L}\cdot\text{atm} = 101.325\text{ J}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
- First law of thermodynamics: \(\Delta U = q + w\).
- Work done during irreversible expansion against constant external pressure: \(w = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V\).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
- Calculate work done in \(\text{L}\cdot\text{atm}\):
\[ w = -2.5 \times (4.50 - 2.50) = -2.5 \times 2.0 = -5.0\text{ L}\cdot\text{atm} \]
- Convert work into Joules:
\[ w = -5.0 \times 101.325\text{ J} = -506.625\text{ J} \approx -505\text{ J} \]
- Calculate \(\Delta U\):
\[ \Delta U = q + w = 0 + (-505\text{ J}) = -505\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
- Expansion work performed by the gas reduces its internal energy in an adiabatic enclosure.
- The change in internal energy \(\Delta U\) is \(-505\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q69 - Maximum volume of container at maximum equilibrium pressure of carbon dioxide

questiontext.text:
A 20 litre container at \(400\text{ K}\) contains \(\text{CO}_2(g)\) at pressure \(0.4\text{ atm}\) and an excess of \(\text{SrO}\) (neglect the volume of solid \(\text{SrO}\)). The volume of the containers is now decreased by moving the movable piston fitted in the container. The maximum volume of the container, when pressure of \(\text{CO}_2\) attains its maximum value, will be
[Given that : \(\text{SrCO}_3(s) \rightleftharpoons \text{SrO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)\), \(K_p = 1.6\text{ atm}\)]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Initial container volume \(V_1 = 20\text{ L}\)
- Initial \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) pressure \(P_1 = 0.4\text{ atm}\)
- Temperature \(T = 400\text{ K}\) (constant)
- Equilibrium constant \(K_p = P_{\mathrm{CO}_2,\text{eq}} = 1.6\text{ atm}\)

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
- Ideal gas behavior for \(\mathrm{CO}_2\).
- Isothermal compression until \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) pressure reaches the maximum equilibrium value \(P_2 = K_p = 1.6\text{ atm}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
- Boyle's law for isothermal gas compression: \(P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2\)

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
- Set \(P_2 = 1.6\text{ atm}\) (maximum achievable pressure before reaction occurs):
\[ 0.4 \times 20 = 1.6 \times V_2 \]
\[ 8 = 1.6 \times V_2 \implies V_2 = \frac{8}{1.6} = 5\text{ litres} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
- Decreasing volume below 5 litres causes \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) to react with \(\mathrm{SrO}\) to form \(\mathrm{SrCO}_3\), maintaining pressure at \(1.6\text{ atm}\). Thus, 5 litres is the maximum volume at which pressure reaches \(1.6\text{ atm}\).
- The maximum volume of the container is \(5\text{ litres}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q70 - Incorrect statement regarding proteins and biological functions

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Biomolecules
Evaluation of protein denaturation, hormonal regulation, storage proteins, and blood clotting factors.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
- Denaturation disrupts higher-order (secondary, tertiary, quaternary) protein structures without breaking primary peptide bonds, causing loss of biological activity. Therefore, stating that denaturation makes proteins more active is incorrect.
- Insulin is a hormone that regulates blood glucose levels.
- Ovalbumin present in egg white functions as a storage protein.
- Thrombin and fibrinogen are essential plasma proteins involved in blood coagulation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement claiming that denaturation makes proteins more active is incorrect.

answer.text: Insulin maintains sugar level in the blood of a human body.
Ovalbumin is a simple food reserve in egg-white.
Blood proteins thrombin and fibrinogen are involved in blood clotting.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q71 - Overall order of reaction from given step wise mechanism

questiontext.text:
Mechanism of a hypothetical reaction \(X_2 + Y_2 \rightarrow 2XY\) is given below :

(i) \(X_2 \rightleftharpoons X + X\) (fast)

(ii) \(X + Y_2 \rightarrow XY + Y\) (slow)

(iii) \(X + Y \rightarrow XY\) (fast)

The overall order of the reaction will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Reaction Mechanism
- Step (i) Equilibrium: \(X_2 \rightleftharpoons 2X\) (fast)
- Step (ii) Rate-determining step: \(X + Y_2 \rightarrow XY + Y\) (slow)
- Step (iii) Fast step: \(X + Y \rightarrow XY\) (fast)

Step 2: Derivation of Rate Law
- Rate law from the slow step (ii):
\[ \text{Rate} = k_2 [X] [Y_2] \]
- From fast pre-equilibrium step (i):
\[ K = \frac{[X]^2}{[X_2]} \implies [X] = K^{\frac{1}{2}} [X_2]^{\frac{1}{2}} \]
- Substitute \([X]\) into rate equation:
\[ \text{Rate} = k_2 K^{\frac{1}{2}} [X_2]^{\frac{1}{2}} [Y_2]^1 = k_{\text{obs}} [X_2]^{0.5} [Y_2]^1 \]

Step 3: Calculation of Reaction Order
- Overall order = sum of powers of concentrations = \(0.5 + 1 = 1.5\).

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
- Rate-determining step involving an intermediate derived from half-order dissociation yields order \(1.5\).
- The overall order of the reaction is \(1.5\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q72 - Identification of oxoanion pair containing sulfur sulfur bonds

questiontext.text: In which pair of ions both the species contain S – S bond?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Analysis of Sulfur Oxoanions
- Tetrathionate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\)): Structure contains a central chain of four sulfur atoms \(\mathrm{O}_3\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\), which possesses \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}\) bonds.
- Thiosulfate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\)): Structure contains a central sulfur atom bonded to a terminal sulfur atom \(\mathrm{S}=\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\), which possesses an \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}\) bond.
- Pyrosulfate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)): Structure is \(\mathrm{O}_3\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\), which contains an \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{S}\) linkage and no \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}\) bond.
- Peroxodisulfate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_8^{2-}\)): Structure is \(\mathrm{O}_3\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\), which contains a peroxide \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{S}\) linkage and no \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}\) bond.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Both \(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\) and \(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\) contain \(\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}\) bonds.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q73 - Identification of species pair with identical bond order

questiontext.text: Which one of the following pairs of species have the same bond order?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Molecular Orbital Theory Principles
Isoelectronic diatomic species (having equal total number of electrons) possess identical molecular orbital configurations and equal bond orders.

Step 2: Total Electron Calculation and Bond Order Determination
- \(\mathrm{CN}^-\): \(6\text{ (C)} + 7\text{ (N)} + 1\text{ (charge)} = 14\text{ electrons}\). Molecular orbital configuration gives bond order = \(3\).
- \(\mathrm{CO}\): \(6\text{ (C)} + 8\text{ (O)} = 14\text{ electrons}\). Molecular orbital configuration gives bond order = \(3\).
- Since both \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) and \(\mathrm{CO}\) are 14-electron isoelectronic species, they have identical bond orders of \(3\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pair \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) and \(\mathrm{CO}\) has the same bond order.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q74 - Antiseptic property of chloroxylenol and terpineol mixture

questiontext.text: Mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol acts as

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Antiseptics are antimicrobial substances applied to living tissues/skin to reduce the possibility of infection, sepsis, or putrefaction.

Step 2: Evaluation of Components
- A mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol is the active composition of Dettol.
- Dettol is a commonly used antiseptic agent safe for application on living human skin and wounds.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol acts as an antiseptic.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q75 - Inert pair effect on oxidation states of tin and lead

questiontext.text: It is because of inability of \(ns^2\) electrons of the valence shell to participate in bonding that

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The inert pair effect refers to the reluctance of valence \(ns^2\) electrons to participate in bonding due to poor shielding by inner \(d\) and \(f\) electrons, increasing down group 14.

Step 2: Stability Analysis for Group 14 Elements
- Down group 14 (\(\mathrm{C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb}\)), the stability of the \(+2\) oxidation state increases while the stability of the \(+4\) oxidation state decreases.
- For tin (\(\mathrm{Sn}\)), the \(+4\) state is more stable than the \(+2\) state. Thus, \(\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\) readily oxidizes to \(\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}\), acting as a reducing agent.
- For lead (\(\mathrm{Pb}\)), due to strong inert pair effect, the \(+2\) state is much more stable than the \(+4\) state. Thus, \(\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}\) readily reduces to \(\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}\), acting as a strong oxidizing agent.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\) is reducing while \(\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}\) is oxidizing.

answer.text: \(\text{Sn}^{2+}\) and \(\text{Pb}^{2+}\) are both oxidising and reducing.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q76 - Temperature threshold for reaction spontaneity

questiontext.text: For a given reaction, \(\Delta H = 35.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) and \(\Delta S = 83.6\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}\). The reaction is spontaneous at : [Assume that \(\Delta H\) and \(\Delta S\) do not vary with temperature]

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Enthalpy change \(\Delta H = 35.5\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = 35.5 \times 10^3\text{ J mol}^{-1}\)
- Entropy change \(\Delta S = 83.6\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}\)
- Condition for spontaneity: \(\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S < 0\)

Step 2: Calculation of Threshold Temperature
- At equilibrium (\(\Delta G = 0\)):
\[ T = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S} = \frac{35.5 \times 10^3\text{ J mol}^{-1}}{83.6\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}} \approx 424.64\text{ K} \approx 425\text{ K} \]
- Since both \(\Delta H > 0\) and \(\Delta S > 0\), the reaction becomes spontaneous (\(\Delta G < 0\)) when \(T \Delta S > \Delta H\), which requires \(T > 425\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Check and Final Answer
- Endothermic reactions with positive entropy change are entropy-driven at higher temperatures.
- The reaction is spontaneous at \(T > 425\text{ K}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q77 - Dependence of molal depression constant on solution concentration

questiontext.text: If molality of the dilute solution is doubled, the value of molal depression constant (\(K_f\)) will be

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Molal depression constant (\(K_f\), cryoscopic constant) is a characteristic thermodynamic property of the solvent.

Step 2: Formula Analysis
- \(K_f\) is given by:
\[ K_f = \frac{R M M_{\text{solvent}} T_f^2}{1000 \Delta H_{\text{fus}}} \]
where \(M_{\text{solvent}}\) is solvent molar mass, \(T_f\) is freezing point, and \(\Delta H_{\text{fus}}\) is enthalpy of fusion of solvent.
- \(K_f\) depends solely on the nature of the solvent and is independent of solute concentration or molality.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Doubling the molality of the solution leaves \(K_f\) unchanged.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q78 - Temperature dependence of solution concentration units

questiontext.text: Which of the following is dependent on temperature ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Concentration expressions involving liquid solution volume vary with temperature because liquid volume expands or contracts upon thermal changes, whereas mass is temperature-independent.

Step 2: Evaluation of Concentration Units
- Molarity \(= \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{volume of solution in L}}\): Dependent on volume, hence temperature-dependent.
- Molality \(= \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}}\): Mass-based, temperature-independent.
- Mole fraction \(= \frac{\text{moles of component}}{\text{total moles}}\): Mass/mole-based, temperature-independent.
- Weight percentage \(= \frac{\text{mass of solute}}{\text{total mass}} \times 100\): Mass-based, temperature-independent.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Molarity is dependent on temperature.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q79 - Hybridization and geometry of hexacyanomanganate III ion

questiontext.text: Pick out the correct statement with respect to \([\text{Mn}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Oxidation State and Electronic Configuration
- Central metal: Manganese (\(\mathrm{Mn}\)), oxidation state \(x + 6(-1) = -3 \implies x = +3\).
- Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Mn}^{3+}\): \([\mathrm{Ar}] 3d^4\).

Step 2: Valence Bond Theory Analysis
- Cyanide (\(\mathrm{CN}^-\)) is a strong field ligand, inducing pairing of the 4 electrons in \(3d\) orbitals into two \(3d\) orbitals.
- This leaves two inner \(3d\) orbitals, one \(4s\) orbital, and three \(4p\) orbitals vacant.
- Hybridization involves six vacant orbitals: \(d^2sp^3\).
- Coordination number is 6, resulting in an octahedral molecular geometry.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\([\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}\) is \(d^2sp^3\) hybridized and octahedral.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q80 - Identification of incorrect statement regarding solid state defects

questiontext.text: Which is the incorrect statement ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Solid State Concepts
- Frenkel defect occurs when smaller ions (usually cations) dislocate from their normal lattice positions into interstitial sites. It is favoured when there is a large difference in size between cations and anions (cation \(\ll\) anion). Stating that Frenkel defect is favoured when cation and anion sizes are almost equal is incorrect (that condition favours Schottky defect).
- \(\mathrm{FeO}_{0.98}\) exhibits non-stoichiometric metal deficiency defect due to missing \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) ions balanced by \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) ions.
- Schottky defect removes equal numbers of cations and anions from lattice sites, lowering density.
- Electrical/mechanical classification of \(\mathrm{NaCl}\), silicon, silver, and quartz is correct.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The statement claiming Frenkel defect is favoured when cation and anion sizes are almost equal is incorrect.

answer.text: Frenkel defect is favoured in those ionic compounds in which sizes of cation and anions are almost equal.
\(FeO_{0.98}\) has non stoichiometric metal deficiency defect.
Density decreases in case of crystals with Schottky's defect.
\(\text{NaCl}(s)\) is insulator, silicon is semi-conductor, silver is conductor, quartz is piezo electric crystal.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q81 - Species formed on dissolving mercuric chloride and iodine in iodide solution

questiontext.text: \(\text{HgCl}_2\) and \(\text{I}_2\) both when dissolved in water containing \(\text{I}^-\) ions, the pair of species formed is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemical Reactions in Solution
- Reaction of \(\mathrm{HgCl}_2\) with excess \(\mathrm{I}^-\) ions forms tetraiodomercurate(II) complex:
\[ \mathrm{HgCl}_2 + 4 \mathrm{I}^- \rightarrow [\mathrm{HgI}_4]^{2-} + 2 \mathrm{Cl}^- \]
- Reaction of elemental iodine \(\mathrm{I}_2\) with \(\mathrm{I}^-\) ions forms triiodide complex ion:
\[ \mathrm{I}_2 + \mathrm{I}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{I}_3^- \]

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The pair of species formed in solution is \(\text{HgI}_4^{2-}\) and \(\text{I}_3^-\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q82 - Recovery method of silver from cyanide leaching solution

questiontext.text: Extraction of gold and silver involves leaching with \(\text{CN}^-\) ion. Silver is later recovered by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Hydrometallurgy
MacArthur-Forrest cyanide process involves dissolving silver ore in dilute \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) in the presence of air to form a soluble cyano complex.

Step 2: Displacement Reaction
- Dissolution step: \(4 \mathrm{Ag} + 8 \mathrm{CN}^- + 2 \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4 [\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2]^- + 4 \mathrm{OH}^-\)
- Recovery step: Metallic silver is precipitated out by displacement using a more electropositive metal such as zinc powder:
\[ 2 [\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2]^- + \mathrm{Zn} \rightarrow [\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_4]^{2-} + 2 \mathrm{Ag} \downarrow \]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Silver is recovered by displacement with zinc.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q83 - Stoichiometry of silver chloride precipitate from cobalt ammine complexes

questiontext.text: The correct order of the stoichiometries of \(\text{AgCl}\) formed when \(\text{AgNO}_3\) in excess is treated with the complexes : \(\text{CoCl}_3\cdot6\text{NH}_3\), \(\text{CoCl}_3\cdot5\text{NH}_3\), \(\text{CoCl}_3\cdot4\text{NH}_3\) respectively is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Werner's Coordination Theory Formulations
- \(\mathrm{CoCl}_3\cdot 6\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_6]\mathrm{Cl}_3\): Has 3 ionizable chloride ions outside coordination sphere, yielding \(3\text{ moles of AgCl}\).
- \(\mathrm{CoCl}_3\cdot 5\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_5\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_2\): Has 2 ionizable chloride ions outside coordination sphere, yielding \(2\text{ moles of AgCl}\).
- \(\mathrm{CoCl}_3\cdot 4\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4\mathrm{Cl}_2]\mathrm{Cl}\): Has 1 ionizable chloride ion outside coordination sphere, yielding \(1\text{ mole of AgCl}\).

Step 2: Final Conclusion
The correct order of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) stoichiometries is \(3\text{ AgCl}\), \(2\text{ AgCl}\), \(1\text{ AgCl}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q84 - Product A and mechanism of 3-bromoanisole with sodamide

questiontext.text:
Identify A and predict the type of reaction

3-bromoanisole \(\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNH}_2}\) A

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction Conditions and Mechanism
- Treatment of 3-bromoanisole (m-bromoanisole) with strong base sodamide (\(\mathrm{NaNH}_2\)) in liquid ammonia occurs via a benzyne intermediate mechanism.
- Elimination of \(\mathrm{HBr}\) generates benzyne intermediate.
- Nucleophilic attack of \(\mathrm{NH}_2^-\) on the benzyne intermediate followed by protonation gives 3-methoxyaniline (m-anisidine) as the major product.
- Since substitution occurs via elimination followed by addition (benzyne mechanism), it is classified as an elimination-addition reaction.

Step 2: Final Conclusion
Product A is 3-methoxyaniline formed via an elimination-addition reaction.

answer.text: and cine substitution reaction

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q85 - Example of sigma bonded organometallic compound

questiontext.text: An example of a sigma bonded organometallic compound is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Organometallic Compounds
- \(\sigma\)-bonded organometallic compounds contain a direct covalent \(\sigma\)-bond between carbon and a metal atom.
- \(\pi\)-bonded organometallic compounds involve bonding between metal atoms and \(\pi\)-electron clouds of organic ligands (metallocenes/sandwich compounds).

Step 2: Evaluation of Options
- Grignard's reagent (\(\mathrm{R-Mg-X}\)): Contains a direct \(\sigma\)-bond between alkyl/aryl carbon and magnesium metal.
- Ferrocene (\(\mathrm{Fe}(\eta^5-\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_5)_2\)), cobaltocene, and ruthenocene are \(\pi\)-bonded metallocene sandwich complexes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Grignard's reagent is an example of a \(\sigma\)-bonded organometallic compound.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q86 - Reason for wide range of oxidation states in actinoids

questiontext.text: The reason for greater range of oxidation states in actinoids is attributed to

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The electronic energy gap between valence subshells determines the participation of electrons in bond formation and oxidation state variability.

Step 2: Evaluation for Actinoids
- In actinoids, the \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) energy levels are very close in energy.
- Because the energy difference between these orbitals is small, electrons from all three subshells (\(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\)) can participate in bonding, leading to a wider spectrum of oxidation states (from \(+3\) up to \(+7\)).
- In lanthanoids, \(4f\) orbitals are much lower in energy than \(5d\) and \(6s\), limiting their oxidation states primarily to \(+3\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The greater range of oxidation states in actinoids is due to \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) levels having comparable energies.

answer.text: 4f and 5d levels being close in energies.

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q87 - Group and electronic configuration of element atomic number 114

questiontext.text: The element \(Z = 114\) has been discovered recently. It will belong to which of the following family group and electronic configuration ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Electronic Configuration of Element Z = 114
- Radon (\(\mathrm{Rn}\)) atomic number = 86.
- Filling sequence after \([\mathrm{Rn}]\) (\(86\)):
\(7s^2\) (2 electrons) \(\rightarrow 88\)
\(5f^{14}\) (14 electrons) \(\rightarrow 102\)
\(6d^{10}\) (10 electrons) \(\rightarrow 112\)
\(7p^2\) (2 electrons) \(\rightarrow 114\)
- Complete outer configuration: \([\mathrm{Rn}] 5f^{14} 6d^{10} 7s^2 7p^2\).

Step 2: Group Identification
- Valence shell configuration \(7s^2 7p^2\) corresponds to Group 14 (Carbon family).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The element belongs to the Carbon family with configuration \([\mathrm{Rn}] 5f^{14} 6d^{10} 7s^2 7p^2\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q88 - Time calculation for first order reaction mass reduction

questiontext.text: A first order reaction has a specific reaction rate of \(10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}\). How much time will it take for \(20\text{ g}\) of the reactant to reduce to \(5\text{ g}\) ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
- Rate constant \(k = 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}\)
- Initial reactant mass \([A]_0 = 20\text{ g}\)
- Final reactant mass \([A]_t = 5\text{ g}\)

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
- First-order integrated rate law:
\[ t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10}\left(\frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}\right) \]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
- Substitute values:
\[ t = \frac{2.303}{10^{-2}} \log_{10}\left(\frac{20}{5}\right) = 2.303 \times 10^2 \log_{10}(4) \]
- Since \(\log_{10}(4) = 2 \log_{10}(2) = 2 \times 0.3010 = 0.6020\):
\[ t = 230.3 \times 0.6020 = 138.64\text{ s} \approx 138.6\text{ second} \]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
- Reducing mass to one-fourth requires 2 half-lives (\(2 \times \frac{0.693}{10^{-2}} = 138.6\text{ s}\)).
- The time required is \(138.6\text{ second}\).

name.text: NEETUG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q89 - Alkali metal ion with lowest ionic mobility in aqueous solution

questiontext.text: Ionic mobility of which of the following alkali metal ions is lowest when aqueous solution of their salts are put under an electric field ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ionic mobility in aqueous medium is inversely proportional to the hydrated ionic radius of the ion.

Step 2: Hydration and Size Comparison
- Down the alkali metal group (\(\mathrm{Li}^+, \mathrm{Na}^+, \mathrm{K}^+, \mathrm{Rb}^+\)), gaseous ionic radius increases.
- \(\mathrm{Li}^+\) has the smallest gaseous ionic size and highest charge density among alkali metal ions.
- Due to high charge density, \(\mathrm{Li}^+\) undergoes maximum hydration in aqueous solution, forming the largest hydrated sphere (\([\mathrm{Li}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_x]^+\)).
- The larger hydrated radius creates higher viscous drag under an electric field, making \(\mathrm{Li}^+\) move slowest.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
\(\mathrm{Li}^+\) ion has the lowest ionic mobility in aqueous solution.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2017_MCQ_Q90 - Relationship between emf values of Daniel cell

questiontext.text:
In the electrochemical cell \(\text{Zn(s)} \mid \text{ZnSO}_4(0.01\,\text{M}) \parallel \text{CuSO}_4(1.0\,\text{M}) \mid \text{Cu(s)}\), the emf of this Daniel cell is \(\text{E}_1\). When the concentration of \(\text{ZnSO}_4\) is changed to \(1.0\,\text{M}\) and that of \(\text{CuSO}_4\) changed to \(0.01\,\text{M}\), the emf changes to \(\text{E}_2\). From the following, which one is the relationship between \(\text{E}_1\) and \(\text{E}_2\)?
\((\text{Given},\, \frac{\text{RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059)\)

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial cell: \(\text{Zn(s)} \mid \text{Zn}^{2+}(0.01\,\text{M}) \parallel \text{Cu}^{2+}(1.0\,\text{M}) \mid \text{Cu(s)}\) with emf \(\text{E}_1\).
Modified cell: \(\text{Zn(s)} \mid \text{Zn}^{2+}(1.0\,\text{M}) \parallel \text{Cu}^{2+}(0.01\,\text{M}) \mid \text{Cu(s)}\) with emf \(\text{E}_2\).
Given constant ratio: \(\frac{\text{RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059\,\text{V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The cell reaction for the Daniel cell is \(\text{Zn(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Cu(s)}\), which involves \(n = 2\) electrons.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
According to the Nernst equation, the cell emf \(E\) is:
\[E = E^\circ - \frac{\text{RT}}{n\text{F}} \ln \left( \frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} \right) = E^\circ - \frac{2.303\,\text{RT}}{n\text{F}} \log_{10} \left( \frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} \right)\]
Using \(\frac{2.303\,\text{RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059\,\text{V}\):
\[E = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} \log_{10} \left( \frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} \right)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For the initial state (\(\text{E}_1\)):
\[\text{E}_1 = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} \log_{10} \left( \frac{0.01}{1.0} \right) = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} \log_{10}(10^{-2})\]
\[\text{E}_1 = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} (-2) = E^\circ + 0.059\,\text{V}\]

For the modified state (\(\text{E}_2\)):
\[\text{E}_2 = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} \log_{10} \left( \frac{1.0}{0.01} \right) = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} \log_{10}(10^2)\]
\[\text{E}_2 = E^\circ - \frac{0.059}{2} (+2) = E^\circ - 0.059\,\text{V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Comparing \(\text{E}_1\) and \(\text{E}_2\): \(\text{E}_1 = E^\circ + 0.059\,\text{V}\) and \(\text{E}_2 = E^\circ - 0.059\,\text{V}\). Therefore, \(\text{E}_1 > \text{E}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q91 - Final proof for DNA as genetic material

questiontext.text: The final proof for DNA as the genetic material came from the experiments of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Although Frederick Griffith demonstrated the bacterial transformation principle in 1928, and Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty later showed that DNA was the transforming agent in 1944, the unequivocal and final proof that DNA is the genetic material was established by Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase in 1952.

Step 2: Evaluation
Hershey and Chase conducted transduction experiments using T2 bacteriophage and Escherichia coli. They labeled viral DNA with radioactive phosphorus (\(^{32}\text{P}\)) and viral protein coats with radioactive sulfur (\(^{35}\text{S}\)). Upon infection, only radioactive \(^{32}\text{P}\) entered the bacterial cells, demonstrating that DNA, not protein, enters bacteria to direct viral replication.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The definitive proof for DNA as the genetic material originated from the experiments of Hershey and Chase.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q92 - Absence of spliceosomes in bacterial cells

questiontext.text: Spliceosomes are not found in cells of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Spliceosomes are ribonucleoprotein complexes present in eukaryotic cells responsible for removing introns from precursor messenger RNA (pre-mRNA) during RNA splicing.

Step 2: Evaluation
Bacterial organisms (prokaryotes) lack split genes containing non-coding introns in their functional structural units; their transcription and translation are coupled processes. Consequently, RNA splicing machinery such as spliceosomes is absent in bacteria. Eukaryotic organisms including plants, fungi, and animals require spliceosomes for post-transcriptional processing.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Spliceosomes are absent in prokaryotic organisms, specifically bacteria.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q93 - Type of joint between atlas and axis

questiontext.text: The pivot joint between atlas and axis is a type of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synovial joints are freely movable joints characterized by a fluid-filled synovial cavity surrounding the articulating surfaces of adjacent bones.

Step 2: Evaluation
A pivot joint is a specific structural type of synovial joint in which a rounded bone rotates within a ring formed by another bone and surrounding ligaments. The atlanto-axial joint between the first cervical vertebra (atlas) and the second cervical vertebra (axis) is a pivot joint, permitting side-to-side rotation of the head.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The pivot joint between the atlas and axis is classified as a synovial joint.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q94 - Structural role of histone H1 in nucleosome

questiontext.text: The association of histone H1 with a nucleosome indicates

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Eukaryotic DNA packaging involves wrapping DNA around histone octamers to form repeating nucleosome units. Histone H1 acts as a linker histone that seals the DNA entry and exit sites on the nucleosome core.

Step 2: Evaluation
The binding of histone H1 facilitates the stabilization and further compaction of nucleosome chains into higher-order chromatin structures, such as the 30 nm chromatin fibre. When DNA undergoes active transcription or replication, histone H1 dissociates to permit unwinding of the double helix.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The association of histone H1 signifies that DNA is packed and condensed into a chromatin fibre.

answer.text: the DNA is condensed into a chromatin fibre.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q95 - Identification of plant tissue composed of dead cells

questiontext.text: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant tissues consist of living or dead cells based on their functional modifications during maturation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Phellem (cork) is produced by the cork cambium (phellogen) during secondary growth. As phellem cells mature, their cell walls become heavily impregnated with suberin, making them impermeable to water and gases, resulting in the loss of protoplasm and cell death. In contrast, phloem sieve elements/companion cells, xylem parenchyma, and collenchyma remain living at maturity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Phellem is composed of dead cells at functional maturity.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q96 - Anatomical route of sperm passage in male frogs

questiontext.text: Select the correct route for the passage of sperms in male frogs

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In male frogs, the reproductive system is connected with the excretory system to form a shared urinogenital passage.

Step 2: Evaluation
Sperms produced in the testes enter 10–12 vasa efferentia, which run to the kidney and open into Bidder's canal. Bidder's canal connects to the urinogenital duct inside the kidney. The urinogenital duct then leaves the kidney to discharge sperms into the cloaca, from where they are released externally.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct anatomical sequence is Testes \(\rightarrow\) Vasa efferentia \(\rightarrow\) Kidney \(\rightarrow\) Bidder's canal \(\rightarrow\) Urinogenital duct \(\rightarrow\) Cloaca.

answer.text: Testes \(\rightarrow\) Vasa efferentia \(\rightarrow\) Kidney \(\rightarrow\) Bidder's canal \(\rightarrow\) Urinogenital duct \(\rightarrow\) Cloaca
Testes \(\rightarrow\) Bidder's canal \(\rightarrow\) Kidney \(\rightarrow\) Vasa efferentia \(\rightarrow\) Urinogenital duct \(\rightarrow\) Cloaca
Testes \(\rightarrow\) Vasa efferentia \(\rightarrow\) Kidney \(\rightarrow\) Seminal Vesicle \(\rightarrow\) Urinogenital duct \(\rightarrow\) Cloaca
Testes \(\rightarrow\) Vasa efferentia \(\rightarrow\) Bidder's canal \(\rightarrow\) Ureter \(\rightarrow\) Cloaca

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q97 - Explanation for enucleated nature of adult human RBCs

questiontext.text:
Adult human RBC's are enucleate. Which of the following statement(s) is/are most appropriate explanation for this feature?
(i) They do not need to reproduce
(ii) They are somatic cells
(iii) They do not metabolise
(iv) All their internal space is available for oxygen transport

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mature mammalian red blood cells lose their nucleus and major organelles during maturation (erythropoiesis) as a functional adaptation.

Step 2: Evaluation
The primary physiological role of red blood cells is the transport of oxygen bound to hemoglobin throughout the circulatory system. Elimination of the nucleus and organelles provides maximal cytosolic space for packing hemoglobin molecules, optimizing oxygen-carrying efficiency. RBCs retain active anaerobic metabolic pathways such as glycolysis, and somatic status or lack of self-replication does not serve as the primary evolutionary driver for enucleation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The primary functional explanation for the absence of a nucleus in adult human RBCs is that all internal space is made available for oxygen transport.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q98 - Method to obtain homozygous pure lines in cattle

questiontext.text: Homozygous pure lines in cattle can be obtained by

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pure lines consist of genetically uniform individuals that are homozygous at key gene loci, established through controlled breeding strategies.

Step 2: Evaluation
Inbreeding—the continuous mating of closely related individuals within the same breed for 4 to 6 generations—increases homozygosity. Selective mating of superior males and females of the same breed over successive generations eliminates undesirable recessive alleles and stabilizes homozygous pure lines.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Homozygous pure lines in cattle are produced by mating related individuals of the same breed.

answer.text: mating of related individuals of same breed.
mating of unrelated individuals of same breed.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q99 - Temporary endocrine gland in human body

questiontext.text: A temporary endocrine gland in the human body is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A temporary endocrine gland is an anatomical structure that develops during a specific physiological state, secretes regulatory hormones into the bloodstream, and subsequently regresses.

Step 2: Evaluation
The corpus luteum forms in the human ovary from the ruptured Graafian follicle following ovulation. It acts as an endocrine structure secreting progesterone and estrogen to prepare and maintain the endometrium for potential pregnancy. If fertilization does not take place, it degenerates into fibrous tissue (corpus albicans) within approximately 10 to 14 days.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The corpus luteum functions as a temporary endocrine gland in humans.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q100 - Structural difference between viroids and viruses

questiontext.text: Viroids differ from viruses in having

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Viroids are sub-viral infectious pathogens that cause disease primarily in plants, possessing a simpler structural organization than viruses.

Step 2: Evaluation
A virus consists of genetic material (either DNA or RNA) enclosed within a protective protein envelope or coat called a capsid. In contrast, a viroid consists exclusively of a short strand of circular, single-stranded RNA devoid of any surrounding protein coat.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Viroids differ from viruses by containing RNA molecules without a protein coat.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q101 - Hormonal response to decreased blood pressure or volume

questiontext.text: A decrease in blood pressure/volume will not cause the release of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Endocrine mechanisms regulate systemic blood pressure and fluid volume through opposing vasoconstrictive/salt-retaining and vasodilatory/salt-excreting pathways.

Step 2: Evaluation
When blood pressure or blood volume drops, the body responds by releasing Anti-Diuretic Hormone (ADH), renin (which triggers aldosterone production), and aldosterone to conserve water and sodium, raising blood pressure. Conversely, Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) is secreted by atrial myocytes in response to high blood pressure or volume expansion to promote sodium excretion (natriuresis) and lower blood pressure.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
A decrease in blood pressure/volume will not trigger the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q102 - Example of colonial alga

questiontext.text: An example of colonial alga is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Algae exhibit distinct morphological organizations including unicellular, colonial, unbranched filamentous, and multicellular parenchymatous forms.

Step 2: Evaluation
Volvox is a green alga that forms hollow spherical colonies (coenobia) containing thousands of interconnected flagellated cells embedded in a mucilaginous matrix. Spirogyra and Ulothrix are unbranched filamentous green algae, while Chlorella is a unicellular non-motile green alga.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Volvox represents a classic example of a colonial alga.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q103 - Morphological nature of edible coconut part

questiontext.text: The morphological nature of the edible part of coconut is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The fruit of a coconut (Cocos nucifera) is a fibrous drupe containing a single large seed with abundant nutritive tissue formed by double fertilization.

Step 2: Evaluation
The edible portion of the coconut consists of triploid endosperm tissue, present both as a liquid free-nuclear endosperm (coconut water) and a solid cellular endosperm (white coconut meat/kernel). The pericarp forms the outer husk and hard shell, whereas perisperm is persistent nucellus tissue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The edible part of a coconut is morphologically the endosperm.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q104 - Correct microbial product matching

questiontext.text: Which of the following is correctly matched for the product produced by them?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific microbial species are commercially exploited to yield valuable biochemicals including ethanol, organic acids, antibiotics, and biogas.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) ferments carbohydrate substrates to produce ethanol.
- Acetobacter aceti oxidizes ethanol to acetic acid.
- Methanobacterium generates methane gas (biogas) anaerobically.
- Penicillium notatum produces the antibiotic penicillin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct match between organism and industrial product is Saccharomyces cerevisiae : Ethanol.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MATCHING_Q105 - Matching sexually transmitted diseases with causative agents

questiontext.text:
Match the following sexually transmitted diseases (Column - I) with their causative agent (Column - II) and select the correct option.

Column - I Column - II
(A) Gonorrhea (i) HIV
(B) Syphilis (ii) Neisseria
(C) Genital Warts (iii) Treponema
(D) AIDS (iv) Human Papilloma virus

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) are caused by specific bacterial, viral, or protozoan pathogens.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Gonorrhea is a bacterial infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
- Syphilis is caused by the spirochete bacterium Treponema pallidum.
- Genital Warts are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV).
- Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is caused by Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct matching set corresponds to (A)-(ii), (B)-(iii), (C)-(iv), and (D)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q106 - Flagellated lining of spongocoel in poriferans

questiontext.text: In case of poriferans, the spongocoel is lined with flagellated cells called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Members of the phylum Porifera (sponges) feature a central cavity known as the spongocoel, through which water flows to facilitate feeding, respiration, and excretion.

Step 2: Evaluation
The interior surface of the spongocoel and associated canals is lined by specialized flagellated collar cells called choanocytes. The beating of choanocyte flagella creates a continuous water current and captures food particles. Mesenchymal cells reside in the gelatinous mesohyl, whereas ostia are incurrent pores and osculum is the excurrent opening.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The flagellated cells lining the spongocoel of poriferans are choanocytes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q107 - Identification of trait not studied by Mendel in garden pea

questiontext.text: Among the following characters, which one was not considered by Mendel in his experiments on pea?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gregor Mendel selected seven distinct pairs of contrasting traits in the garden pea (Pisum sativum) for his hybridization experiments.

Step 2: Evaluation
The seven character pairs analyzed by Mendel were stem height (tall/dwarf), seed shape (round/wrinkled), seed color (yellow/green), pod shape (inflated/constricted), pod color (green/yellow), flower color (violet/white), and flower position (axial/terminal). Glandular or non-glandular trichomes were not among the character pairs studied by Mendel.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Trichome morphology (glandular or non-glandular) was not considered by Mendel.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q108 - Incorrect statement regarding heartwood properties

questiontext.text: Identify the wrong statement in context of heartwood

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In old trees, secondary xylem becomes differentiated into central heartwood (duramen) and peripheral sapwood (alburnum).

Step 2: Evaluation
Heartwood consists of dead, highly lignified elements infiltrated with organic compounds such as tannins, resins, gums, and essential oils, making it hard and durable. However, due to occlusion of vessel lumens by tyloses and chemical deposits, heartwood loses transport capacity and does not conduct water and minerals. Conduction of water and minerals is carried out exclusively by sapwood.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement claiming that heartwood conducts water and minerals efficiently is incorrect.

answer.text: It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q109 - Direction of Okazaki fragment elongation during DNA replication

questiontext.text: During DNA replication, Okazaki fragments are used to elongate

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
DNA polymerases synthesize DNA strands strictly in the \(5' \rightarrow 3'\) direction relative to the new strand.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because the antiparallel template strands unwind at the replication fork, continuous synthesis occurs on the leading strand toward the fork. On the template strand with \(5' \rightarrow 3'\) polarity relative to fork movement, synthesis proceeds discontinuously as short segments called Okazaki fragments. These fragments elongate the lagging strand in the \(5' \rightarrow 3'\) direction, moving away from the replication fork.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Okazaki fragments serve to elongate the lagging strand away from the replication fork.

answer.text: the lagging strand away from the replication fork.
the leading strand towards the replication fork.
the lagging strand towards the replication fork.
the leading strand away from the replication fork.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q110 - Ecological interaction represented by mycorrhizae

questiontext.text: Mycorrhizae are the example of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mutualism is a symbiotic interspecific interaction in which both participating species derive obligatory or facultative physiological benefits.

Step 2: Evaluation
Mycorrhiza represents a symbiotic association between fungal hyphae and the roots of higher plants. The fungal partner absorbs essential inorganic nutrients (particularly phosphorus) from soil for the plant, while the plant supplies energy-rich organic carbohydrates synthesized via photosynthesis to the fungus.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Mycorrhizae exemplify mutualism.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q111 - Most abundant RNA type in animal cells

questiontext.text: Which of the following RNA's is the most abundant in animal cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cellular RNA species fulfill structural, catalytic, and informational roles, differing significantly in intracellular concentration.

Step 2: Evaluation
Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) constitutes approximately 80% of total RNA in eukaryotic cells due to the vast number of ribosomes required for protein synthesis. Transfer RNA (tRNA) accounts for roughly 15%, messenger RNA (mRNA) comprises 3–5%, and microRNAs (miRNA) represent a very small fraction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Ribosomal RNA (r-RNA) is the most abundant RNA species in animal cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q112 - Term for protein separation and purification

questiontext.text: The process of separation and purification of expressed protein before marketing is called

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Recombinant DNA technology includes upstream operations (gene cloning and fermentation) and downstream processing (product recovery).

Step 2: Evaluation
Once a target protein is biosynthesized in bioreactors, it must be harvested, isolated, purified, stabilized, and formulated into a commercial product. These post-expression isolation and purification stages are collectively called downstream processing.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The separation and purification of expressed proteins before marketing is downstream processing.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q113 - Smallest cell wall less pathogenic prokaryotes

questiontext.text: Which among the following are the smallest living cells, known without a definite cell wall, pathogenic to plants as well as animals and can survive without oxygen?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Certain prokaryotic organisms lack a rigid cell wall, enabling variable cell morphology and survival in anaerobic environments.

Step 2: Evaluation
Organisms belonging to the genus Mycoplasma are the smallest known living cells (0.1–0.3 \(\mu\text{m}\)). They lack a cell wall entirely, exhibit pleomorphism, function as facultative anaerobes, and cause diseases in both plants and animals. Nostoc, Bacillus, and Pseudomonas possess rigid peptidoglycan cell walls.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The described organisms are Mycoplasma.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q114 - Bacterial envelope layer providing stickiness

questiontext.text: Which of the following components provides sticky character to the bacterial cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The bacterial cell envelope is a complex multi-layered structure comprising an outer coating, a cell wall, and an inner plasma membrane.

Step 2: Evaluation
The glycocalyx is the outermost layer of sticky polysaccharides or polypeptides secreted outside the cell wall. It forms either a loose slime layer or a dense capsule, allowing bacteria to adhere to surfaces, host cells, and form biofilms, as well as protecting against immune phagocytosis.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The glycocalyx provides sticky characteristics to bacterial cells.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q115 - Incorrect statement regarding factors affecting photosynthesis

questiontext.text: With reference to factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis, which of the following statements is not correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photosynthetic rates depend on environmental factors including light intensity, \(\text{CO}_2\) concentration, and ambient temperature, which interact differently in \(\text{C}_3\) and \(\text{C}_4\) plant pathways.

Step 2: Evaluation
\(\text{C}_4\) plants possess PEP carboxylase and a \(\text{CO}_2\)-concentrating mechanism, allowing them to exhibit a higher temperature optimum (\(30^\circ\text{C} - 40^\circ\text{C}\)). In contrast, \(\text{C}_3\) plants have a lower temperature optimum (\(20^\circ\text{C} - 25^\circ\text{C}\)) because elevated temperatures increase oxygenase activity of RuBisCO and promote photorespiration. Thus, stating that \(\text{C}_3\) plants respond to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis while \(\text{C}_4\) plants have a much lower optimum is false.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement asserting that \(\text{C}_3\) plants show enhanced photosynthesis at higher temperatures relative to \(\text{C}_4\) plants is incorrect.

answer.text: Tomato is a greenhouse crop which can be grown in \(\text{CO}_2\)-enriched atmosphere for higher yield.
Light saturation for \(\text{CO}_2\) fixation occurs at 10% of full sunlight.
Increasing atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) concentration upto 0.05% can enhance \(\text{CO}_2\) fixation rate.
\(\text{C}_3\) plants responds to higher temperatures with enhanced photosynthesis while \(\text{C}_4\) plants have much lower temperature optimum.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q116 - Enzyme composition of pancreatic juice

questiontext.text: Which of the following options best represents the enzyme composition of pancreatic juice?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pancreatic juice is an alkaline exocrine secretion containing digestive enzymes for carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids.

Step 2: Evaluation
Pancreatic juice contains lipases, pancreatic amylase, trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidase, and nucleases. Pepsin and rennin are acidic digestive enzymes secreted by gastric glands, whereas maltase and enterokinase are components of intestinal juice (succus entericus).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The enzyme combination consisting of Lipase, amylase, trypsinogen, and procarboxypeptidase accurately represents pancreatic juice.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q117 - Structural formula relation of holoenzyme

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is correct, with reference to enzymes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Conjugated enzymes (haloenzymes) consist of a protein moiety bound to a non-protein cofactor or coenzyme.

Step 2: Evaluation
The inactive protein component of a conjugated enzyme is termed the apoenzyme. When it combines with an organic non-protein cofactor (coenzyme) or inorganic ion, it forms the complete, catalytically active enzyme called a holoenzyme:
\[\text{Holoenzyme} = \text{Apoenzyme} + \text{Coenzyme}\]

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct relationship is \(\text{Holoenzyme} = \text{Apoenzyme} + \text{Coenzyme}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q118 - Calculation of altered codons due to frameshift deletion

questiontext.text: If there are 999 bases in an RNA that codes for a protein with 333 amino acids, and the base at position 901 is deleted such that the length of the RNA becomes 998 bases, how many codons will be altered?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial length of RNA: 999 bases (coding for 333 codons / amino acids).
Deletion position: base at position 901.
Final length of RNA: 998 bases.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
A codon consists of a triplet sequence of 3 nucleotides. Deletion of a single base causes a reading frame shift for all subsequent codons downstream from the point of deletion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The bases up to position 900 remain unchanged. The affected region starts at position 901 and extends to the 999th original base.
Number of affected bases = \(999 - 901 + 1 = 99\) bases.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Divide the number of affected bases by 3 to find the number of altered triplet codons:
\[\text{Altered codons} = \frac{99}{3} = 33\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Codons 1 through 300 (bases 1–900) remain intact. Codons 301 through 333 (bases 901–999) undergo frameshift mutation. Thus, exactly 33 codons are altered.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q119 - Condition for asymptote in logistic population growth

questiontext.text: Asymptote in a logistic growth curve is obtained when

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Logistic population growth accounts for finite environmental resources and carrying capacity (\(K\)), modeled by the Verhulst-Pearl logistic equation.

Step 2: Evaluation
The differential equation for logistic growth is:
\[\frac{dN}{dt} = rN \left(1 - \frac{N}{K}\right)\]
When the population size \(N\) reaches the environmental carrying capacity \(K\) (\(N = K\)), the factor \(\left(1 - \frac{N}{K}\right)\) becomes zero. Consequently, the population growth rate \(\frac{dN}{dt}\) drops to zero, and the growth curve reaches a stable horizontal plateau known as an asymptote.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
An asymptote in a logistic growth curve occurs when population size equals carrying capacity (\(K = N\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q120 - Mismatched pair of plant spore/sexuality characteristics

questiontext.text: Select the mismatch from the following

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant reproductive structures exhibit monoecious (bisexual) or dioecious (unisexual) organization and homosporous or heterosporous spore production.

Step 2: Evaluation
- Equisetum is a homosporous pteridophyte.
- Cycas is a dioecious gymnosperm with distinct male and female plants.
- Salvinia is a heterosporous aquatic fern.
- Pinus is a monoecious gymnosperm because both male strobili (pollen cones) and female strobili (seed cones) develop on different branches of the same tree. Pairing Pinus with dioecious is therefore a mismatch.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The mismatched pair is Pinus – Dioecious.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q121 - Cellular consequence of defective anaphase promoting complex

questiontext.text: Anaphase promoting complex (APC) is a protein degradation machinery necessary for proper mitosis of animal cells. If APC is defective in a human cell, which of the following is expected to occur?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Anaphase-Promoting Complex/Cyclosome (APC/C) is an ubiquitin ligase that targets specific cell-cycle regulators for proteasomal degradation during the metaphase-to-anaphase transition.

Step 2: Evaluation
APC/C targets securin for destruction, which frees the protease separase to cleave cohesin protein complexes holding sister chromatids together. If APC is defective, securin remains intact, separase remains inactive, cohesin is not cleaved, and sister chromatids fail to separate. As a result, chromosomes will not segregate to opposite poles during anaphase.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
A defective APC causes chromosomes to fail to segregate.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q122 - Ecosystem type with maximum standing biomass

questiontext.text: Which ecosystem has the maximum biomass?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biomass refers to the total mass of living organic matter accumulated per unit area within an ecosystem at a given time.

Step 2: Evaluation
Forest ecosystems are dominated by massive, long-lived woody perennial trees that accumulate immense amounts of organic structural tissue (trunk, roots, branches). Consequently, terrestrial forest ecosystems exhibit a much higher standing biomass per unit area compared to aquatic ecosystems (lakes, ponds) or grassland ecosystems dominated by herbaceous plants.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Forest ecosystems possess the maximum biomass.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q123 - Organism characterized by zygotic meiosis

questiontext.text: Zygotic meiosis is characteristic of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In haplontic life cycles, the main vegetative body is haploid, and the diploid stage is restricted solely to the unicellular zygote.

Step 2: Evaluation
In Chlamydomonas (a green alga), syngamy produces a diploid zygote that undergoes immediate meiotic division (zygotic meiosis) to generate four haploid zoospores. In bryophytes like Marchantia and Funaria, sporic meiosis occurs within the multicellular sporophyte. In Fucus (a brown alga), a diplontic life cycle occurs with gametic meiosis.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Zygotic meiosis is characteristic of Chlamydomonas.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q124 - Cause for lack of height increase in adult hypersecretion of growth hormone

questiontext.text: Hypersecretion of Growth Hormone in adults does not cause further increase in height, because

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Elongation of long bones occurs at specialized hyaline cartilage regions called epiphyseal plates located between the diaphysis and epiphyses.

Step 2: Evaluation
During adolescence, rising sex steroid levels promote the calcification and complete fusion (closure) of epiphyseal plates with the shaft of long bones. After epiphyseal plate closure, long bones lose the capacity for linear longitudinal extension. Consequently, excess growth hormone in adults stimulates periosteal appositional growth leading to bone thickening (acromegaly) rather than an increase in overall stature.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hypersecretion of growth hormone in adults does not increase height because epiphyseal plates close after adolescence.

answer.text: muscle fibres do not grow in size after birth.
bones loose their sensitivity to Growth Hormone in adults.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q125 - Myogenic and autoexcitable nature of frog heart

questiontext.text:
Frog's heart when taken out of the body continues to beat for sometime.
Select the best option from the following statements:
(i) Frog is a poikilotherm
(ii) Frog does not have any coronary circulation
(iii) Heart is "myogenic" in nature
(iv) Heart is autoexcitable

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The cardiac tissue of amphibians possesses inherent contractility capable of generating rhythmic action potentials independently of external neural signals.

Step 2: Evaluation
The frog heart continues to beat outside the body because it is myogenic (the contractile impulse originates within modified cardiac muscle cells rather than nerve fibers) and autoexcitable (specialized nodal tissue spontaneously initiates action potentials without external nerve stimulation). Poikilothermic temperature regulation and coronary vascular patterns do not account for isolated cardiac beating.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The sustained beating of an isolated frog heart is explained by its myogenic and autoexcitable properties.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2017_MCQ_Q126 - Immune response responsible for organ transplant rejection

questiontext.text: Transplantation of tissues/organs fails often due to non-acceptance by the patient's body. Which type of immune-response is responsible for such rejections ?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The immune system distinguishes between self and non-self cells primarily through major histocompatibility complex (MHC) markers displayed on cell surfaces.

Step 2: Evaluation
Graft rejection following organ transplantation is primarily driven by cell-mediated immunity. T-lymphocytes recognize foreign MHC/HLA antigens present on the donor tissue and initiate cytotoxic responses that destroy the graft. Humoral immunity plays a secondary role, while physiological mechanisms do not drive rejection.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Cell-mediated immune response is responsible for organ graft rejections.
